prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System = Regional Flow Platform (Cedarbell). Airports Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport keep safety authority. TOBT=Target Off Block Time: issued only if capacity/ground path allow; frozen at horizon unless exception recorded; revised only on turnaround-actor confirmation. Modes: Normal Operations; Adverse Weather Mode (Duty Manager may reduce remote stands); Recovery Phase (remote stands absorb late arrivals); Capacity Reduction State (Registry tightens escalation); Contingency Fallback State (Contingency Operations Console). Elements: Demand Prediction Service (Marlinstone; predicted readiness; AAR=Airport Acceptance Rate); Capacity Assessment Module (CAM; classifies sector overload as departure/arrival/mixed; fix saturation=planned departures by fix vs Airport Capacity Plan; Registry thresholds split short peak vs sustained saturation -> Tactical Regulation Proposal); Slot Allocation Engine (Blueharbor; CTT=Calculated Takeoff Time; Ground Delay Program equity plus local priority); Departure Metering Service (Emberline); North/South Runway Meters; Surface Surveillance Adapter; East/West Apron Sensors; Airport CDM Portal (Foxglove; Collaborative Decision Log records reasons when border/customs/apron data change sequencing or stands); Tower Sequence Manager (TSM, Ironleaf; SHALL NOT advance aircraft unless remote stand release supports taxi plan); Gate Conflict Detector; Airline Interface Adapter; Handling Resource Planner; Alert Distribution Hub (Lantern; MUST meet latency; alerts on customs hold vs stand plan, apron sensing vs off-block milestone); Ramp Movement Board (Skylark; MUST refresh apron layer within 5 s); Audit Event Ledger; Business Rules Registry; Sector Load Monitor (counts, predicted occupancy, overload flags; Departure Fix Load Sheet to Regional Flow Manager); Flight Data Exchange (scheduled movements); Performance Analytics Warehouse (planned vs actual border release/apron); Time Synchronization Service; Arrival Regulation Console (Nightjar); Data Governance Steward (border/customs access/retention rules); Weather Ingest Gateway (Orchard); Digital… Conversion: departure overload -> departure rate, fix allocation or runway spacing; arrival -> adjusted AAR or metered stream to Nightjar; mixed -> paired measures. Short peak -> TSM sequence advisory or metering adjustment; sustained -> revised CTT and TOBT via CDM Portal.

New part:
S604: The Airline Operations Coordinator reviews the airport-level result to determine whether flight swaps, cancellations, or recovery plans are needed inside the airline schedule.
S605: The Tower Supervisor uses the same result to understand whether a runway queue is being held for surface capacity, runway capacity, or downstream airspace capacity.
S606: The Surface Surveillance Adapter produces the Runway Lighting Outage Card when monitored runway lighting status affects a declared operating configuration.
S607: En-route constraints received from network coordination are normalized into constraint records with an affected route, start time, end time, expected capacity, and confidence value.
S608: The Airspace Sector Planner validates the operational meaning of each constraint before it is allowed to influence airport rates.
S609: The Military Airspace Liaison confirms whether conditional route availability changes the effective capacity before the constraint is converted to a local measure.
S610: Weather-related en-route limitations are correlated with information from Weather Ingest Gateway so that airport measures reflect both sector capacity and route availability.
S611: In Normal Operations, the conversion may only produce monitoring alerts because sector demand remains below the action threshold.
S612: In Adverse Weather Mode or Capacity Reduction State, the same inputs are allowed to produce binding metering values, revised rates, and additional coordination tasks.
S613: All converted measures are displayed on Common Situation Display with the source constraint, effective interval, affected runway or fix, and expected delay impact.
S614: Alert Distribution Hub sends notifications to Regional Flow Manager, Tower Supervisor, Ramp Control Lead, Slot Coordinator, and Network Operations Liaison when a measure changes operational behavior.
S615: Collaborative Decision Log records the constraint, chosen conversion rule, responsible actor, and time of approval for traceability.
S616: Performance Analytics Warehouse later compares predicted sector pressure, actual airborne delay, and airport departure compliance to tune Demand Prediction Service and Capacity Assessment Module.
S617: Crew legality is represented in the Regional Flow Platform as operational constraints rather than as detailed employment records.
S618: The Airline Interface Adapter accepts legality indicators that describe whether a proposed departure, arrival, or aircraft swap remains feasible within declared crew duty limits.
S619: The model uses time thresholds, qualification flags, and pairing feasibility status, but it does not require names, pay rules, hotel arrangements, or internal crew roster details.
S620: Aircraft Operator Representative sends the Crew Duty Extension Log when an approved company process extends duty availability for a specific rotation.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
